entities.name: Define the user algebra promotion frontier
entities.summary: Separate library theory, surface ergonomics, kernel necessity, and runtime capabilities for resource, concurrency, and STM algebras.

acceptance: Promotion decisions keep userland, surface, kernel, and runtime layers distinct
Users receive an explicit minimum workbench for authoring and discovering algebras
Resource lifecycle laws distinguish finalization from mathematical inversion
Structured concurrency uses one-shot continuations and scope-owned children
STM retains both owner-actor and shared-memory realization paths
Kernel promotion requires an established elaboration obstruction

relations.summary: The accepted kernel is the elaboration target whose sufficiency must be tested.
The accepted surface compiler provides the current syntax and elaboration baseline.
STM promotion waits for explicit concurrency, resource, and runtime-substrate classification.
Alternative runtime realizations and promotion gates inform the STM library decision.
